course.title: SciPy — From Beginner to Professional
course.description: A visual-first, practice-led SciPy curriculum following the supplied 40-page course blueprint: 136 ordered topics across 20 modules, 28 practical exercises, 12 portfolio projects, optional specialist extensions, and a reproducible capstone workflow. Content is draft pending review.
course.version_scope: Prepared against the official SciPy 1.18.0 manual surfaced as the current manual on 2026-10-17. The available local runtime used for content validation reports SciPy 1.17.0; examples are therefore not claimed to have been executed against SciPy 1.18.0. Re-run examples and read the relevant release notes before publication.
prerequisites: Basic Python syntax, functions, loops, modules, and exceptions.
A working understanding of NumPy arrays, shapes, dtypes, and broadcasting.
Basic algebra is essential; calculus, probability, linear algebra, and differential equations are introduced or reviewed before dependent advanced topics.
learning_outcomes: Choose appropriate SciPy algorithms based on the scientific question, assumptions, and input structure.
Use SciPy to solve numerical integration, differentiation, optimization, interpolation, linear algebra, statistical, signal, spatial, image, and differential-equation tasks.
Validate results with residuals, tolerances, error estimates, solver diagnostics, tests, and independent checks.
Build reproducible scientific workflows with documented dependencies, units, data provenance, and limitations.
Distinguish current APIs from legacy interfaces and check release notes for compatibility.

recommended_learning_path.title: Orientation and setup
recommended_learning_path.milestone: Create an isolated environment, import SciPy, and reason about NumPy arrays and numerical precision.

recommended_learning_path.title: Numerical foundations
recommended_learning_path.milestone: Use constants, special functions, derivatives, linear systems, and matrix diagnostics.

recommended_learning_path.title: Core numerical methods
recommended_learning_path.milestone: Integrate, solve ODEs, interpolate data, find roots, optimize objectives, and fit models.

recommended_learning_path.title: Signal and data-analysis methods
recommended_learning_path.milestone: Analyze signals, design filters, select statistical methods, and report uncertainty.

recommended_learning_path.title: Specialized scientific algorithms
recommended_learning_path.milestone: Choose sparse, spatial, image, clustering, file-I/O, and ODR tools for appropriate problems.

recommended_learning_path.title: Professional workflow
recommended_learning_path.milestone: Compose reusable pipelines, test numerical behavior, improve performance, and reproduce results.

recommended_learning_path.title: Application and capstone
recommended_learning_path.milestone: Deliver a tested numerical project with justified methods, reproducible settings, and documented limitations.
